targetReport.title: Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP 2018)
targetReport.description: The UN's standard classification for household consumption expenditure. Deliberately not minted for the Canada or US CPI slices already in the graph (`international-frameworks.json`'s own dropped notes: StatCan's CPI never uses COICOP at all, and BLS only produces a COICOP mapping as a side series for the OECD, not something the headline release rests on -- 'It should return if a document is found where COICOP governs a primary release.'). South Africa is that document: Stats SA's own CPI Sources and Methods report states 'The South African CPI adopted the 2018 version of the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) for goods and services with effect from the January 2025 publication' -- COICOP 2018 is the actual basket structure of the live release, not a side output.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised on a multi-decade cycle (prior editions predate 2018 by a similar span to SNA's revision cadence); not an annual release.

release_schedule.note: Next revision is contingent on the outcome of the separate COFOG revision process (targeted 2028) rather than its own independent schedule.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

targetReport.title: Agreement on the New Development Bank (Fortaleza, 15 July 2014) and annexed Articles of Agreement
targetReport.publisher: Governments of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People's Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
targetReport.description: Foundational treaty establishing the New Development Bank (NDB). Signed in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014 by the five founding BRICS members. Entered into force 3 July 2015 after all five deposited instruments of acceptance/ratification. Russia ratified by Federal Law No. 29-FZ of 8 March 2015. Creates the Bank, sets purpose (mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development in BRICS and other EMDCs), capital structure (initial authorised USD 100 bn, subscribed USD 50 bn), governance, and membership rules. Continuously cited as the legal basis in every subsequent NDB Annual Report, strategy document, and project approval.
